title: Write a city's ratio rules as linear rows

blocks.text: A city transit agency splits its maintenance budget across its modes: bus, rail and ferry. The council has passed two kinds of rule, both written as ratios:

items: no mode gets more than a share `max_share` of the total spent;
for each pair `(a, b, ratio)` in `pairs`, mode `a` gets at least `ratio` times what mode `b` gets (the council wrote it as "a / b must be at least ratio").

blocks.text: With $`K`$ the modes, $`x_k \ge 0`$ the amount spent on mode $`k`$, $`\alpha`$ the largest share and $`P`$ the pairs, the rules are:

Neither is linear as written. Multiply each one out first (every amount is $`\ge 0`$), then write `add_share_rules(model, spend, max_share, pairs)` in `rules.py`: it adds one row per mode and one row per pair to `model`, where `spend` maps each mode to its variable. Name the rows `share_<mode>` and `ratio_<a>_<b>`.
The tests fix every amount to a plan's value and ask GLOP whether your rows allow it, so any correct linear form passes. About five lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from rules import add_share_rules

AREAS = ("parks", "roads", "libraries")


def allowed(plan, max_share, pairs):
    """Fix every amount to the plan's value and ask GLOP whether the rows allow it."""
    model = mathopt.Model()
    spend = {k: model.add_variable(lb=plan[k], ub=plan[k], name=k) for k in AREAS}
    add_share_rules(model, spend, max_share, pairs)
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.GLOP)
    return result.termination.reason == mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL


print("plan 30/40/30, share 0.4:", allowed({"parks": 30, "roads": 40, "libraries": 30}, 0.4, []))
print("plan 20/55/25, share 0.4:", allowed({"parks": 20, "roads": 55, "libraries": 25}, 0.4, []))
pairs = [("parks", "libraries", 1.5)]
print("plan 30/40/30, share 0.4, parks >= 1.5 libraries:", allowed({"parks": 30, "roads": 40, "libraries": 30}, 0.4, pairs))

cases.says: a split with every mode under its share is allowed, and one with a mode far above it is refused
the share is of the whole total, the mode's own spend included
every mode is held to the share, not only the first one listed
a pair (a, b, ratio) bounds a from below by ratio times b, not the other way round
multiplying the ratio out puts the ratio on the second mode's side, so a ratio below 1 allows the first mode less than the second

origin.section: Every Rule Is One Linear Row, and a Ratio Is Multiplied Out Before It Is Written

concepts: a share or ratio rule becomes a linear row once both sides are multiplied by a total that is never negative
